channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: China to heavily restrict AI export
item.description: China has proposed tighter export controls on 40 technologies, with 14 facing outright bans and 26 requiring official approval before transfer abroad.

item.title: Four European countries sign free trade agreement with Vietnam
item.description: The agreement covers trade in goods and services, intellectual property rights, trade defence measures and sustainable development.

item.title: European Council leaves Ukraine in uncertainty about delivery of anti-ballistic interceptors
item.description: “We’ll keep on living – living with dignity – and fighting.”

item.title: Pope Leo XIV fit to be discharged from hospital
item.description: The Pope had surgery to remove a cancerous lung nodule. He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon.

item.title: Anthropic to put forward AI safety law
item.description: The company behind the renowned Claude AI model is adamant they can enforce new safety laws that could potentially change AI's trajectory for the foreseeable future.

item.title: IMF and World Bank express 'optimism and concern' after annual meeting
item.description: Debt repayments in low-income countries have risen from 8% to 14% of government revenue, as higher energy prices and inflation deepen pressure on the poorest economies.

item.title: UN fails to agree on climate science report
item.description: In a post on LinkedIn, France's climate envoy warned about the "costly lost time" in publishing the latest update as the UN tackles climate change.

item.title: Asylum applications in Belgium fall for ninth consecutive month, outpacing European decline
item.description: The number of asylum applications in Belgium has fallen for the ninth consecutive month compared with last year, with the decline significantly sharper than across the European Union.

item.title: The EU engages with the Taliban regime to deport migrants amid human rights concerns
item.description: “The question is if it is indeed safe to return anyone to Afghanistan under the Taliban rule.”

item.title: Belgian police raid houses of family members of Congolese president Tshisekedi
item.description: Belgian police raided the houses of multiple family members of Félix Tshisekedi on Wednesday, as part of an investigation into money laundering.

item.title: EU’s foreign affairs council steps up pressure on Russia and involvement in the Middle East
item.description: “We are making it significantly harder, slower, and more expensive for Russia to produce weapons it uses to kill Ukrainians.”

item.title: Palestinian students: Why Belgium does not enable them to leave Gaza for studies
item.description: "It has become increasingly clear to us is that preventing us from coming to Belgium is a political decision."

item.title: International Energy Agency urges extra diesel release
item.description: The agency warned the situation needs “immediate attention,” urging countries to speed up undelivered oil releases and prioritise diesel if more supply support is needed.

item.title: EU defence commissioner calls for Ukraine strategy after Trump's attack
item.description: The bloc’s defence chief said the EU has been Ukraine’s only serious financial backer, as warnings grow that easing pressure on Moscow could help fund the war.

item.title: Poland reports assassination ploy against prime minister
item.description: The threat alert comes days after the prime minister warned that a “culture of violence” had reached Poland, amid growing concern over attacks involving minors in schools.

item.title: European security agencies warned about Russian sabotage plans
item.description: Security costs are rising as defence executives respond to alleged Russian plots, while officials warn that even amateurish plans can spread fear and deter business with Ukraine.

item.title: Last migrant camp dismantled in Ceuta after summer crisis
item.description: Police and soldiers cleared the last large camp in Ceuta days before a royal visit, after more than 70,000 people crossed into the enclave in two days and dozens died.

item.title: Royal couple heads to Kazakhstan for state visit
item.description: Their stay will mark the first-ever Belgian state visit in the Central Asian country.

item.title: Germany continues to work with EU on Russian sanctions
item.description: After Donald Trump lifted the Russian diesel ban and will restart supply on a global level, the EU is still working on further sanctions.

item.title: Ireland proposes €140 billion EU budget cut
item.description: Ireland has proposed cutting the next long-term EU budget by 8%, or €141bn, while protecting farm and regional funds in an effort to bridge deep divisions among member states.
